toc.title: How the Developers Conduct a Daily Scrum (CSM 1.12)
How the Daily Scrum Differs from a Status Meeting (CSM 1.13)
The Daily Scrum, the Sprint Backlog and the Sprint Goal
Exam Traps and What the Exam Expects

html:
1Purpose, Participants and Rules

Item What the Guide says
Purpose "To inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary, adjusting the upcoming planned work"
Who "A 15-minute event for the Developers of the Scrum Team"
When and where "To reduce complexity, it is held at the same time and place every working day of the Sprint"
Product Owner and Scrum Master "If the Product Owner or Scrum Master are actively working on items in the Sprint Backlog, they participate as Developers"
Structure "The Developers can select whatever structure and techniques they want, as long as their Daily Scrum focuses on progress toward the Sprint Goal and produces an actionable plan for the next day of work. This creates focus and improves self-management"
Benefits Daily Scrums "improve communications, identify impediments, promote quick decision-making, and consequently eliminate the need for other meetings"
Not the only time "The Daily Scrum is not the only time Developers are allowed to adjust their plan. They often meet throughout the day for more detailed discussions about adapting or re-planning the rest of the Sprint's work"
Exam angle

the Daily Scrum is the Developers' event. Its purpose is to plan the next day's work toward the Sprint Goal, not to report status to the Scrum Master, the Product Owner or a manager. It lasts 15 minutes whatever the Sprint length.

2How the Developers Conduct a Daily Scrum (CSM 1.12)

The Guide leaves the format to the Developers. A typical flow that satisfies its rules Beyond the Guide:

Step What the Developers do
1. Gather At the same time and place, in front of the Sprint Backlog
2. Inspect Look at progress toward the Sprint Goal: what is finished, what is in progress, what is at risk
3. Adapt Change the Sprint Backlog and the plan: reorder, split, swap who works on what, add or drop tasks (never the Sprint Goal)
4. Plan the next day Leave with an actionable plan for the next day of work
5. Raise impediments Say what blocks progress, so that it can be removed (the Scrum Master causes the removal)
6. Close within 15 minutes Move deeper conversations to a follow-up among the people concerned

2.1 Ways to structure it Beyond the Guide

Format How it works Note
Walk the board Go through the Sprint Backlog item by item, usually from the item closest to Done Keeps the focus on the work, not on people
By Sprint Goal Ask what stands between the team and the Sprint Goal today Strong link to the goal
Discussion-based Free discussion focused on the plan for the day Needs discipline
Three questions Each person answers what they did toward the goal, what they will do, and what blocks them An example, not a requirement
Old wording

The 2017 Guide listed three questions as an "example of what might be used": "What did I do yesterday that helped the Development Team meet the Sprint Goal? What will I do today ...? Do I see any impediment ...?" The 2020 Guide removed them and says only that the Developers choose their own structure and techniques. It also dropped the 2017 duties of the Scrum Master ("ensures that the Development Team has the meeting ... teaches the Development Team to keep the Daily Scrum within the 15-minute time-box ... If others are present, the Scrum Master ensures that they do not disrupt the meeting") and the phrase "held every day of the Sprint" (now "every working day").

2.2 Who else may attend?

The Guide describes the event as one "for the Developers" and gives no role to anyone else except the Product Owner and Scrum Master as Developers. It neither requires nor describes observers. The Scrum Master still ensures that the events take place and are positive, productive and kept within the timebox (Topic 5). Anyone who wants to know the status can see the Sprint Backlog and the Increment, and the Sprint Review is the event for stakeholders.

3How the Daily Scrum Differs from a Status Meeting (CSM 1.13)

The objective asks for at least three differences Beyond the Guide, built on the Guide's rules.

Daily Scrum Status meeting
Purpose Plan the next day of work toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog Report on past work and compare it with a plan
Whose event The Developers', for themselves A manager's or project manager's, who receives the reports
Direction of information Developers talk to each other Each person reports up to someone who oversees the work
Outcome An actionable plan for the next day, an updated Sprint Backlog, impediments raised A status report, updated tracking, assigned follow-ups
Structure Chosen by the Developers Set by the manager (round-robin, fixed agenda)
Focus The Sprint Goal Individual tasks, hours and percent complete
Decisions Made quickly by the Developers Often escalated or made by the manager
Control Supports self-management Supports oversight

3.1 Why the constraints support the Developers

Constraint (from the Guide) How it supports the Developers
15-minute timebox Keeps the event short and focused; detailed discussions happen afterwards between the people who need them; saves time for the work
Same time and place every working day Reduces complexity: no scheduling effort, and a habit that all rely on
For the Developers Gives them ownership of their plan and a safe place to be honest about problems; no reporting up
Focus on the Sprint Goal Keeps the team working together on one objective instead of separate initiatives
Produces an actionable plan for the next day Turns inspection into adaptation, which is the point of the event
Developers choose structure and techniques Builds self-management and lets the format change as the team learns

4The Daily Scrum, the Sprint Backlog and the Sprint Goal

  • The Daily Scrum is the Developers' inspection point for the Sprint Backlog, which is "a highly visible, real-time picture of the work" and should have "enough detail that they can inspect their progress in the Daily Scrum".
  • The Developers adapt the plan (the Sprint Backlog). The Sprint Goal does not change (Topic 11). If the work is different from what they expected, they negotiate scope with the Product Owner within the Sprint, without affecting the Sprint Goal.
  • Adaptation is "the moment [the team] learns anything new through inspection" and "as soon as possible" (Topic 1).

5Common ProblemsBeyond the Guide

Problem Better practice
Each person reports to the Scrum Master or the Product Owner Developers talk to each other about the plan
The event runs over 15 minutes Park deeper topics for a follow-up conversation
Time and place change Fix them
Nothing changes after the event End with an actionable plan and an updated Sprint Backlog
Reporting yesterday only Look forward: what must happen today and tomorrow toward the Sprint Goal
The Scrum Master runs it The Developers run it; the Scrum Master ensures it takes place

6Exam Traps and What the Exam Expects

  1. Purpose: inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog. Status reporting is wrong.
  2. Fifteen minutes whatever the Sprint length, every working day, at the same time and place.
  3. The Developers' event. The Product Owner and Scrum Master take part only as Developers, when actively working on Sprint Backlog items.
  4. The Developers choose structure and techniques. The three questions are an old example, not a rule.
  5. The Scrum Master does not run it and does not collect status. The Scrum Master ensures it takes place and stays within the timebox.
  6. The output is an actionable plan for the next day of work.
  7. Impediments are raised and the Scrum Master causes their removal. The Daily Scrum is not where they are solved in depth.
  8. Detailed discussions happen afterwards, among the people who need them. The Developers often meet throughout the day.
  9. The Sprint Goal does not change at the Daily Scrum. The plan does.
  10. The Daily Scrum can eliminate other meetings. Adding extra status meetings goes against it.
  11. Old wording "Development Team", "internal meeting", "the three questions", "every day of the Sprint" and the Scrum Master teaching the Development Team to keep the 15-minute time-box are 2017 wording.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Scenario questions (choose the best answer)

S1The Product Owner asks each Developer to report individual status at the Daily Scrum, to update the stakeholders. What should the Scrum Master do?

  • AAllow it, because the Product Owner is accountable for the product and must keep the stakeholders informed every day about what each Developer has done
  • BExplain that the Daily Scrum is the Developers' event to plan the next day toward the Sprint Goal; status is in the Sprint Backlog
  • CAsk the Developers to write individual status reports for the Product Owner instead of reporting in person
  • DCancel the Daily Scrum, as the Product Owner already knows the status of every Developer after each report
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute event for the Developers whose purpose is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog. Status for stakeholders is visible in the Sprint Backlog and inspected at the Sprint Review. Reporting individual status turns it into a status meeting.

S2A discussion about a design problem makes the Daily Scrum run to 40 minutes every day. What is the best action?

  • AExtend the Daily Scrum to 40 minutes
  • BHave the Product Owner decide the design
  • CStop the Daily Scrum until the problem is solved
  • DKeep the Daily Scrum to 15 minutes and let the people concerned continue the discussion afterwards
Show the answer

Answer: D. The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute event, and the Developers often meet throughout the day for more detailed discussions about adapting or re-planning. The timebox keeps the event focused. Extending it or stopping it loses its purpose.

S3A new team is told that every Daily Scrum must follow the three questions "what did I do yesterday, what will I do today, what is blocking me". What does the 2020 Guide say?

  • AThey were an example in the 2017 Guide; the Developers may choose any structure that focuses on progress toward the Sprint Goal
  • BThe three questions are mandatory in every Daily Scrum, so a team that uses another structure is not doing Scrum
  • CThe Scrum Master chooses the questions for each Daily Scrum and makes sure that every Developer answers all of them in turn within the fifteen minutes
  • DThe Product Owner sets the agenda of the Daily Scrum, because the Product Owner is accountable for the progress
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Developers can select whatever structure and techniques they want, as long as the event focuses on progress toward the Sprint Goal and produces an actionable plan for the next day. The three questions were an example in the 2017 Guide and were removed in 2020.

S4The Daily Scrum is held at a different time and place each week, depending on who is free. What does the Guide suggest?

  • AThis is fine: flexibility matters most
  • BThe Scrum Master decides each week
  • CHold it at the same time and place every working day, to reduce complexity
  • DHold it only when there are impediments
Show the answer

Answer: C. To reduce complexity, the Daily Scrum is held at the same time and place every working day of the Sprint. Regularity is part of its design.

S5What is the purpose of the Daily Scrum?

  • ATo report the status of each Developer to the Scrum Master
  • BTo inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog, adjusting the upcoming planned work
  • CTo plan the next Sprint
  • DTo review the Increment with stakeholders
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Guide states this purpose exactly. Reporting status, planning the next Sprint and reviewing the Increment belong elsewhere or are not Scrum events.

S6A manager asks how the Daily Scrum differs from the weekly status meeting that the team previously held. Which answer is best?

  • AThe Daily Scrum is shorter than the weekly status meeting, but otherwise the two events serve the same purpose
  • BThe Daily Scrum has more people attending, so that decisions can be taken faster than in a weekly status meeting
  • CThe Daily Scrum replaces the Retrospective, because the team inspects how it works every day rather than once at the end of the Sprint
  • DIt is the Developers' own planning event toward the Sprint Goal, not a report to a manager; it yields a plan for the day
Show the answer

Answer: D. A status meeting reports to someone overseeing the work. The Daily Scrum is run by the Developers for the Developers, focuses on the Sprint Goal and produces an actionable plan. Length alone is not the difference.

S7Several managers want to attend every Daily Scrum to hear progress. What is the best way to meet their need?

  • AShow them the Sprint Backlog and the Increment and invite them to the Review; the Daily Scrum is the Developers' event
  • BMake the Daily Scrum a report to them, so that they hear each Developer's progress directly each morning
  • CAdd a second status meeting for the managers right after the Daily Scrum, so the Developers also keep their own
  • DAsk the Developers to email daily progress reports to the managers, so that the managers need not attend
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Daily Scrum is for the Developers, and the Sprint Backlog is a highly visible, real-time picture of the work. The Sprint Review is the event where the Scrum Team and stakeholders inspect results. An extra status meeting contradicts the aim to eliminate other meetings.

S8At the Daily Scrum, two Developers realize that they need an hour to settle how to integrate their work. What should they do?

  • ASpend the hour inside the Daily Scrum, since the integration problem blocks both Developers and the rest of the team
  • BAsk the Scrum Master to decide how the work should be integrated, since the Scrum Master has seen the problem
  • CFinish the Daily Scrum in 15 minutes and let the two Developers meet separately for the detailed discussion
  • DSkip the discussion, as integration problems are normally solved by themselves during the Sprint
Show the answer

Answer: C. The Developers often meet throughout the day for more detailed discussions about adapting or re-planning the work. The Daily Scrum stays within 15 minutes, and the discussion does not wait.

S9The Scrum Master is also working on a Sprint Backlog item. Must the Scrum Master attend the Daily Scrum?

  • AYes, as a Developer, because the Scrum Master is actively working on items in the Sprint Backlog
  • BNo, the Scrum Master may never attend, because the Daily Scrum is reserved for the Developers
  • CYes, in order to run the meeting and to record each Developer's progress for the Product Owner
  • DOnly if the Product Owner asks for it, since the Product Owner is accountable for the Sprint's progress
Show the answer

Answer: A. If the Product Owner or Scrum Master are actively working on items in the Sprint Backlog, they participate as Developers. Otherwise the event is for the Developers.

7.2 Recall Q&As

R1What is the purpose of the Daily Scrum?

Show the answer

To inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary, adjusting the upcoming planned work.

R2How long is the Daily Scrum?

Show the answer

15 minutes.

R3When and where is it held?

Show the answer

At the same time and place every working day of the Sprint.

R4For whom is it?

Show the answer

The Developers of the Scrum Team.

R5When do the Product Owner and Scrum Master take part?

Show the answer

If they are actively working on items in the Sprint Backlog, as Developers.

R6Who chooses the structure and techniques?

Show the answer

The Developers.

R7What must the Daily Scrum focus on and produce?

Show the answer

It must focus on progress toward the Sprint Goal and produce an actionable plan for the next day of work.

R8What are the benefits of the Daily Scrum?

Show the answer

Improved communication, impediments identified, quick decision-making, and less need for other meetings.

R9Is the Daily Scrum the only time the Developers can adjust their plan?

Show the answer

No. They often meet throughout the day for more detailed discussions about adapting or re-planning.

R10Name three differences between the Daily Scrum and a status meeting.

Show the answer

Purpose (plan versus report); whose event (the Developers' versus a manager's); direction (to each other versus upward); outcome (an actionable plan versus a report); structure chosen by the Developers; focus on the Sprint Goal.

R11Why does the 15-minute timebox support the Developers?

Show the answer

It keeps the event focused and short, leaves detailed discussions for those who need them and protects time for the work.

R12What happened to the three questions in 2020?

Show the answer

They were an example in the 2017 Guide and were removed; the Developers choose their own structure.

R13Does the Daily Scrum change the Sprint Goal?

Show the answer

No. It adapts the Sprint Backlog and the plan toward the Sprint Goal.

R14What is the timebox of the Daily Scrum in a two-week Sprint?

Show the answer

15 minutes.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Purpose Inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal; adapt the Sprint Backlog
Length 15 minutes, every Sprint
When and where Same time and place, every working day
Who The Developers; Product Owner or Scrum Master only as Developers if working on Sprint Backlog items
Structure Chosen by the Developers; must focus on the Sprint Goal and produce an actionable plan for the next day
Benefits Communication, impediments, quick decisions, fewer other meetings
Beyond the event Developers meet during the day for detailed discussions
Versus status meeting Plan not report · Developers' own · to each other not upward · actionable plan · Sprint Goal focus
Constraints support Focus, ownership, self-management, no scheduling overhead
Scrum Master Ensures it takes place and is kept within the timebox; does not run it or collect status
Old wording Three questions, "internal meeting", Scrum Master teaches the time-box (2017)
